Haderslev is a Danish municipality evaluated in the 2022–2023 Annual Report from the Danish Atrial Fibrillation Database (Databasen for Atrieflimren i Danmark), published by the Regions' Clinical Quality Improvement Programme (RKKP) [^src1] [^src2]. The report assesses the clinical quality of atrial fibrillation treatment across all 98 Danish municipalities, focusing on key indicators such as anticoagulation therapy coverage, early treatment initiation, and safety monitoring [^src1] [^src2]. 

In the context of Indicator 4b, which measures adherence to safety practices regarding the use of DOAC (Direct Oral Anticoagulant) medications, Haderslev achieved a notably high compliance rate [^src1]. The municipality met the standard for this indicator, marked as "Yes," with a score of 95.9% (1,069 out of 1,115 eligible cases), placing it among the highest-performing entities in the report [^src1]. The 95% confidence interval for this metric was recorded as 94.5% to 97.0% [^src1]. 

Additionally, Haderslev is evaluated on other clinical metrics within the report, such as the prevention of ischemic stroke (Indicator 5) and early initiation of anticoagulation treatment (Indicator 1) [^src2]. For one such metric detailed in the municipal breakdown, Haderslev recorded a rate of 0.2% (with a confidence interval of 0.0% to 0.6%) and a secondary metric of 0.5% (8 out of 1,483 cases) [^src2]. These detailed, localized breakdowns underscore Haderslev's role in the decentralized responsibility for clinical quality development and benchmarking within the Danish healthcare system [^src1] [^src2].
